newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cambodia may export small amount of rice in 2001.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia may export small amount of rice in 2001.

text.p: Cambodia, ravaged by decades of war that only recently ended, is now self-sufficient in rice and should be able to export a small amount of about 700,000 tonnes in 2001, an official from its Agriculture Ministry said on Friday.
Baden Cameron, senior policy adviser to the ministry, said in a report to the Asia rice conference in Singapore that Cambodia produced 3.3 million tonnes of rice in 1995.

"Although a modest increase in regional supply, it is of great significance to the Cambodian economy as agriculture by then will still represent 40 percent of national gross domestic product," he said.
The rice yield in Cambodia currently stands at 1.3 tonnes a hectare, low in comparison to the 2.1 tonnes a hectare of Thailand or the 3.2 tonnes per hectare in Vietnam.
